whats_new.text: U.S.–China summit in Washington ends with no public breakthrough on Taiwan; the ~$14B U.S. arms package for Taiwan is still on hold.

Washington rejects an Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; two U.S. carriers (George Washington, George H.W. Bush) stay on the CENTCOM blockade — they now start the game in the Arabian Sea, committed for 2 turns.

situation.summary: Tense but not at war: Washington and Beijing talked without a Taiwan deal, the U.S. keeps two carriers on the Iran blockade far from the Pacific, and the Western Pacific carrier is heading home.

flashpoints.title: Summit ends, arms package still held
flashpoints.text: The U.S.–China summit ended without a public Taiwan breakthrough. Taipei says arming Taiwan is an important U.S. interest; the U.S. ambassador in Beijing says Taiwan policy is unchanged. The ~$14B U.S. arms sale remains under review amid U.S. stockpile and industrial-base limits. Beijing's party paper calls Taiwan its 'core of core interests'.

flashpoints.title: 16 PLA aircraft and ships around Taiwan
flashpoints.text: Taiwan's defense ministry tracked 5 PLA aircraft, 6 navy ships and 5 official ships in 24 hours; one aircraft crossed the median line into the northern ADIZ. No named large exercise.

flashpoints.title: U.S. rejects Iran's Hormuz offer
flashpoints.text: Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and pause wider fighting in exchange for lifting the port blockade, frozen funds and oil sanctions. Washington said no. The conflict has run since late February; CENTCOM reports 110 commercial ships redirected by the blockade.

src.title: Where Are The Aircraft Carriers?: September 23, 2026

flashpoints.title: ADMM-Plus drills in the West Philippine Sea
flashpoints.text: A Philippines-led sea phase on Sept 23 with 11 ships from the Philippines, U.S. (USS Canberra), Japan (JS Ise), Australia (HMAS Perth), India, New Zealand, Singapore and Brunei. China attended the opening but not the sea phase.

flashpoints.title: Long-range strike war intensifies
flashpoints.text: At least 16 killed in 24 hours of cross-strikes. Ukraine hit refineries in Krasnodar and Ilsky; Russian drones and missiles hit Kyiv. Ukraine reports 205 front-line clashes a day, heaviest near Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk. Ukrainian air defense stops about 55% of Russia's jet drones.

briefs.text: The ~$14B Taiwan arms package was still on hold and the summit produced no Taiwan deal.

events.title: Hormuz stays shut
events.text: Washington rejects Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Tankers keep queuing; war-risk premiums climb.

events.title: Taiwan arms package still frozen
events.text: The ~$14B sale stays under review — U.S. stockpiles and factories are stretched across three theaters.

events.title: Summit ends, no Taiwan deal
events.text: Beijing repeats that Taiwan is its 'core of core interests'. Washington says its policy is unchanged. Markets shrug; militaries don't.

events.title: Eight navies drill in the West Philippine Sea
events.text: ADMM-Plus warships from the Philippines, U.S., Japan, Australia, India, New Zealand, Singapore and Brunei sail together. China stays away.

events.title: PLA probes around Taiwan
events.text: Aircraft, warships and coast guard hulls ring the island; one jet crosses the median line. Taiwan scrambles fighters and coastal missiles.

events.title: Interceptors spread thin
events.text: Russia's drone-and-missile waves on Ukraine keep draining air-defense stocks. Every PAC-3 fired in Europe is one fewer for the Pacific.

events.title: Refinery strikes rattle oil markets
events.text: Long-range drones hit Russian refineries while Kyiv is struck again. Fuel prices tick up worldwide.
